title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
We are typically beginner to intermediate levels playing in a friendly, sociable, and supportive environment while not being shy to a little friendly competition! We may rally freely in the beginning to warm up and then move on to some quick-rotation matches between 5-7 points. No formal teams here so everyone should be ready to both play with and against everyone else who shows up.

If you’re going to show up later than 8 AM then please tell us in the comments. Otherwise by signing up you agree to show up at 8 AM by default! Also, if you’re running late for any reason then please tell us in the comments – just make sure you’re not driving at the time and please always drive safely!

Also please be sure to bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those! Also, I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own as well in case we need to branch out over more than one court!

Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make serious plans to attend then please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible for their own decision to take a break, even if it has to be in the middle of a match! So health first, fun second, friendly competition third!

title: Creative Liturgy Workshop
description:
The prayers we recite by rote each week were not handed down fully formed from heaven—they were written by real people, reaching for words to express their hopes and fears, their loves and losses. Over time, those personal prayers became the shared liturgy of the Jewish people. But sometimes, the ancient words of others don’t quite resonate, which is why the process of prayer writing must be ongoing. Join Rabbi James Feder once a month to explore new liturgy being written for our current moment and take a hand at writing some yourself.

title: The Joyful Art of Paper Folding NEW
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a free Adult School class. Click below to register.

In the Philippines, the young and the old love paper folding. They feel a sense of connection with their family and community by folding single sheets of paper to create beautiful objects, presenting them as thoughtful, handmade gifts for loved ones.

Paper folding is an enjoyable, creative, and meditative art form: transforming flat pieces of paper to three-dimensional objects. Through hands-on demonstrations and one-on-one instructions, students will learn and make simple to intricate structures, creating toys, flowers, birds, and utilitarian objects.

An accessible art, suitable for beginners and experienced folders, paper folding promotes mindfulness and relaxation. It improves fine and gross motor skills, spatial perception, and has other cognitive benefits.

title: Vintage Crawl & Record Fair
location: Lackawanna Station, Montclair, NJ 07042, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
The Montclair Vintage Crawl is a town-wide treasure hunt for anyone who loves the thrill of finding something with a story. 
Start your weekend at Lackawanna Station, where the Big Room kicks things off with a curated lineup of vintage dealers, vinyl sellers, and open tables where guests are invited to show off their own finds or take a turn DJing. Pick up your map here — it’s your passport for the rest of the crawl. 
From there, head into the Little Shops tucked inside Lackawanna Station for stop #2, then follow the map out across Montclair to every participating vintage shop in town. Snap a photo at each stop along the way. Complete the crawl, return to Lackawanna Station with your photos, and claim your prize. 
You’ve got all weekend to do it. Come for an hour or come for two days. The map is yours and the town is open.

title: Daytime Pool at Black Diamond Billiards
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
***Much like last time, trying something different. Unlike Clifton Billiards, this place has its own parking lot. They only do $20 day passes, but it's super laid back, we don't have to check in with management to change tables, and we can play as long as we want. This place also lets people bring their own food and drink, so if we want to order from a local spot, bring snacks or beverages, we are able. \*\*\* Expectations\*\*:
Pool cues are available at the location, expect mid to low lighting.
\*\* *What if I'm a beginner or only want to play with people at a similar level?*\*
Tables will be divided between beginners, intermediate players, and advanced. However, this depends on how many types of players come, so it will be divided as best as possibly available. \*\*\* I feel like people aren't trying to be my friend.\*

description: Very (very) excited to present this quartet of contemporary heavyweights. Seed Artists founder PHEEROAN AKLAFF is one of the pre-eminent drummers in modern jazz. Vibraphonist/composer/educator CHRIS DINGMAN, a former student of Pheeroan's at Wesleyan University, worked extensively with Herbie Hancock and Wayne Shorter and is a leading light on the instrument. LA-based saxophonist/composer and Cal Arts professor STEVE LEHMAN is one of the most important figures in contemporary jazz. A musician's musician and a composer of startling originality. And we are thrilled to bring back STOMU TAKEISHI, master of the fretless electric bass, whose many credits include Don Cherry, Henry Threadgill, Pat Metheny, Randy Brecker, and Butch Morris. Expect creative music at the highest level.

description:

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
We are typically beginner to intermediate levels playing in a friendly, sociable, and supportive environment while not being shy to a little friendly competition! We may rally freely in the beginning to warm up and then move on to some quick-rotation matches between 5-7 points. No formal teams here so everyone should be ready to both play with and against everyone else who shows up.

If you’re going to show up later than 8 AM then please tell us in the comments. Otherwise by signing up you agree to show up at 8 AM by default! Also, if you’re running late for any reason then please tell us in the comments – just make sure you’re not driving at the time and please always drive safely!

Also please be sure to bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those! Also, I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own as well in case we need to branch out over more than one court!

Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make serious plans to attend then please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible for their own decision to take a break, even if it has to be in the middle of a match! So health first, fun second, friendly competition third!
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: Schuylkill River Series: Pottstown-Royersford
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this point to point hike, the next in our Schuylkill series, between Pottsville and Royersford.
After meeting at Royersford, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to the start.
We'll start by following a small creek greenway, then a bit of Schuylkill River Trail, but we must deviate from it because the 422 crossing is not yet open.
We'll use parallel roads on the opposite side of the river including another couple of parks and a cemetery to get to the next bit of the trail.
We'll continue along the trail, but deviate a couple of times to check out different side trails. We will be doing the Sanatoga Preserve as well as Independence Park Trail, then the Royersford Trestle to the end.
Distance will be about 15 miles. If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374.

location: Montclair - Offsite, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

In 1776, while the 13 colonies were rising up against Britain, the rest of North America was occupied by a mixture of empires competing through an interconnected web of conquest, exploration, settlement and trade. From the Spanish missions in California to Native American trade centers on the Missouri River, Captain Cook’s voyage up the Pacific Coast in search of the Northwest Passage, Russian forays to Alaska for sea otter pelts, the Hudson Bay Company’s quest for fur-trade dominance, and the expanding Plains empire of the Comanche, we will explore how diverse peoples shaped a continent in flux. Maps, images and discussion will illuminate the year 1776 as both a revolutionary and continental turning point in the story of North America.

title: Marcel Duchamp: The Alchemist of the Avant Garde - Online NEW
location: Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.
Open the dictionary to the word “iconoclast,” and you will see a picture of Marcel Duchamp. He challenged the standards and beliefs of the art world and ushered in a new era of creative license—the reverberations of which are still felt in contemporary art today. Duchamp’s imagination was aroused by elements of Cubism, Surrealism, and even Pop Art, but his resourcefulness meant continuous self-reinvention and deliberate inconsistency. He once said, “I have forced myself to contradict myself in order to avoid conforming to my own taste.” Come and learn about his innovative works and the shockwaves they produced. A blockbuster Duchamp retrospective will be up at the Museum of Modern Art from April 12 to August 22.

title: Parent Academy Series School Year 2025-2026
description:
The Parent Academy is an engaging monthly program that runs September through June where parents and caregivers can learn practical tools and strategies to support their youth’s mental well-being. Each session focuses on a specific mental health topic and provides helpful resources and tips that can be used right away. 
These sessions are psychoeducational webinars, not to be used in place of clinical treatment. 
TOPICS: 
Suicide Prevention – Wednesday 9/17 12-1:00pm
Developed by the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention, the session is designed to help parents, teachers, and other caring adults recognize the warning signs of suicide in youth, initiate conversations around depression and suicidal thoughts, and guide them in helping young people access needed support and resources.  
Teen Dating Violence: Visible & Voiced – Tuesday 10/21 6:30-7:30pm
This session equips parents with the tools to recognize signs of dating violence in teens and respond with confidence. Learn how to spot red flags, support open communication, and help your teen build safe, healthy relationships.  
Less Stress, More Joy: Holiday Prep for Parents – Wednesday 11/12 12-1:00pm
This interactive webinar will help you plan for a more peaceful and meaningful holiday season. NJ4S will share simple strategies and practical tools to help you set healthy boundaries, manage stress, and prioritize your well-being.  
Spotting the Signs: A Guide to Youth Substance Use Awareness – Tuesday 12/9 12-1:00pm
PRESENTED BY Center for Prevention and Counseling
Participants will be equipped with tools and knowledge to recognize and respond to youth substance use.  
Suicide & Social Media – Wednesday 1/21 6:30-8:00pm
PRESENTED BY Jonathan Singer Ph.D., LCSW
This webinar will translate the most important research on social media and suicide risk into practical tips.  
Eating Disorders 101 – Tuesday 2/24 6:30-7:30pm
Information, signs to recognize, and resources will be shared on the topics of anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, and binge-eating disorders.  
High Stakes: The Rising Risk of Youth Gambling – Tuesday 3/10 12-1:00pm
PRESENTED BY New Bridge Services Information will be shared about the growing issue of youth gambling, shedding light on trends, what to look for, and available resources.  
Parent/Caregiver Support for Children on the Spectrum – Tuesday 4/21 6:30-7:30pm 
The session will provide a safe, supportive, and empowering space for parents/caregivers of children on the autism spectrum to connect, share topics, and build resilience through tools for mental health, self-care, and caregiving.  
A Parent’s Guide to Youth Mental Health – Wednesday 5/13 6:30-7:30pm
This webinar will focus on the various aspects of mental health, how to have the conversation with a youth in your life, and what to expect after the conversation.  
Bored to Brave: Building Independence through Community Adventures this Summer – Tuesday 6/2 12-1:00pm
This webinar will cover the impact of changing schedules, empowering youth to reduce screen time, and creating opportunities within the home, neighborhood, and community. Our NJ4S summer programs will be noted, as well as free resources within the counties.

Engage in this interactive session designed to bring forth your inner storyteller with confidence! Registration is required.

Ana Cristina Coura, is an educator with a background in psychology who has taught children in Brazil and worked as an art educator.



Sabina Wasonga-Gitau is an educator and a storyteller. She is a native Swahili speaker. Her interest in sharing her culture has led her to infuse the Swahili language in her storytelling. She is a Folk artist with The Folklife Center of Northern New Jersey. A recipient of the New Jersey State Council on the Arts (Folk Arts Apprenticeship Grant). She has told stories  online and in person at Public Libraries, Colleges, Middle Schools and Elementary Schools. She has performed at the UN during World Kiswahili Day and at the Montclair Literary Festival. She believes everyone has a story.

location: Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:

Burnout is a serious issue affecting many of us. It is characterized by fatigue, low productivity and feeling disconnected at work. The effects of burnout extend beyond personal challenges; they can negatively impact overall health, leading to higher absenteeism, high turnover rate, workplace conflicts and low job satisfaction. title: Rock Voices Montclair: Three Open-House Opportunities - come sing with our Community Rock Choir!
location: 153 Park St, Montclair, NJ 07042, 153 Park St., Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
If you’ve been missing how much fun it is to sing with other people – or always wanted to try it out for the first time – come check out Rock Voices Montclair as we get our Summer 2026 “MUSIC FROM THE MOVIES” Season started! 
We are a fun and friendly community choir for adults – with an emphasis on community – and we sing only ROCK, pop, and other contemporary music. There are never any auditions required to join, and ALL ARE WELCOME. Rock Voices has 35+ chapters across the Northeast US and Portland, and we’ve been making music in Montclair since the Fall of 2023. 
We rehearse on Tuesday nights from 7-9pm in Montclair, with our next season starting on May 19th, and a Summer Concert in August. Enrollment for the season is open through June 8th. (We also record all of our rehearsals, so if you’ve already got some warm-weather vacay plans in the mix, no worries at all – we’ve got you covered with as many replays as needed!) 
This season’s Open House Rehearsal dates are 5/19, 5/26, and 6/2 – please join us at one, two, or all three, as we start our 12-week session. There’s no obligation with these Open Houses, so just come hang out with us – have some snacks, make some new friends, sing some songs you probably know…and see what you think! 
You can check out our full set list for the season at www.RockVoices.com – and you can sign up there too, just so we know to look out for you, and to have enough sheet music (and snacks!) ready. Plus it’ll be faster than waiting in line to do it when you get there. 
Here’s our direct link: https://rockvoices.com/choir_location/montclair-nj/ 
Please follow us on FB, IG, and YouTube @RockVoicesMontclairNJ to learn more about us, and to find our FB event page and Enrollment FAQs too – we hope to sing with you soon!

description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: Scalable Cross-Region Disaster Recovery Models for Ensuring High Availability
description:
Cloud Data Driven
This session explores scalable cross-region disaster recovery (DR) models for maintaining high availability in modern cloud data platforms. It evaluates active-active, active-passive, and hybrid architectures using a simulation-based framework, analyzing key metrics such as Recovery Time Objective (RTO), Recovery Point Objective (RPO), availability, and cost.

The findings highlight critical trade-offs: active-active models offer near-zero downtime but high complexity and cost, while active-passive and hybrid approaches are more cost-efficient but introduce recovery delays and potential data inconsistency. The study emphasizes the need for adaptive, workload-aware DR strategies rather than one-size-fits-all solutions.

The topic is highly relevant in today’s world, where geopolitical conflicts and incidents such as the destruction of data centers during the recent war in the middle east demonstrate the importance of resilient, geographically distributed cloud infrastructure for ensuring business continuity.

By the end of this session, attendees will be able to:

\- Understand the fundamentals of cross\-region disaster recovery and its role in ensuring high availability in distributed cloud systems

\- Differentiate between active\-active\, active\-passive\, and hybrid architectures\, including how they operate under failure conditions

\- Analyze key disaster recovery metrics such as Recovery Time Objective \(RTO\) and Recovery Point Objective \(RPO\)\, and interpret their impact on system performance and business continuity

\- Evaluate trade\-offs between cost\, latency\, consistency\, and operational complexity when selecting a disaster recovery strategy

\- Apply practical insights to design resilient\, scalable cloud architectures capable of handling real\-world disruptions\, including large\-scale outages and infrastructure failures

description:

Only 10 attendees allowed social distancing and mandatory mask wearing.

You are invited to participate in a special session of creative thinking and fresh insight dedicated to inspiration.

We live in a world of constant change that requires us to be able to continually adapt and innovate in order to succeed. Unfortunately, many of us have forgotten how to delve into our raw creativity and leave behind the rigidity of the frameworks we have progressively interiorized.
This unique workshop seeks to reclaim our inspiration and imagination, rethink the unthinkable. It is ideal for people working in the creative arts as well as students, entrepreneurs, team managers, corporate leaders and anyone looking to implement their creative vision.

Inspiration is a vital driving force in our lives that moves us to create our best work and lights the way for new, authentic ideas. How do we invite, cultivate and harness inspiration so that we are able to bring these ideas into reality?
As a self-taught artist exploring various avenues of self-expression, Issa Sow draws a distinction between the phenomenon of inspiration itself and our task of making ourselves ready for it.
In the upcoming Inspiration Trap workshop, we will imagine ways we can invite and contain our inspiration, and well as keep our mind in the open, dynamic state as a receptacle or a “canvas” to collect, reflect and grow our ideas.
Feel free to bring along a personal object, a piece of clothing or even a small piece of furniture to play with during this hands-on experiment in innovative thinking. There are surprises and new elements in each session!

title: Roses to Rock Gardens Tour 2026
location: Van Vleck House & Gardens, 21 Van Vleck Street, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
Step inside some of the most beautiful private gardens in and around Montclair—spaces you wouldn’t normally get to see. Each stop on the Roses to Rock Gardens Tour offers something different: lush rose gardens in full bloom, thoughtfully designed landscapes, hidden backyard retreats, and creative plantings that reflect the personalities of the people who care for them. Whether you’re a serious gardener, a design lover, or just someone who enjoys a beautiful afternoon outdoors, this tour is a chance to gather ideas, inspiration, and a fresh appreciation for what a garden can be. 
Start your day at Van Vleck House & Gardens, then explore at your own pace. We have 9 fabulous private gardens to visit! Also stop at Avis Campbell Gardens, which is lovingly tended by The Garden Club of Montclair and celebrating their 100th anniversary this year. title: Simple Sitting Meditation
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Bowling Night - North Jersey
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
This is an event for casual bowling at Montvale Lanes, 14 W. Grand Ave. All are welcome for **two games, food and drinks**, and any post- or pre-game hang out. Show up anytime! Questions or comments? You can message Andy Milone on Meetup, or call/text him at **201-234-9609**.

\*\*\* Before bowling, we might stop by the Pizza Parlour, 6 S. Kinderkamack Road in Montvale, for a few slices. Post a comment on the event page to gauge interest. **After bowling, we'll definitely be heading to Davey's Irish Pub & Restaurant, 5 Park St. in Montvale, or The Ridge Diner, 125 Kinderkamack Road in Park Ridge, at 10 p.m. for some food and/or drinks.** \*\*\*

About the group: People of all ages, backgrounds and abilities are welcome! We're not professionals and we're not in a league. In fact, we're a group of people who probably each won't score more than 100 points and will land more than our fair share of gutter balls. There's no pressure at all!!!! We're not here to analyze your form or technique.

More event details: You pay for your own games, food and drinks. Please bring cash. The alley does not accept card. But there is an ATM on site. **The** **cost per player is $18 for two games** **and bowling shoes.** If you have your own shoes, the cost is $12. Please try to bring exact change since Andy will have a limited amount of cash. If you bring a $20 bill and he doesn't have change, any remainder would just go toward the bowling alley tip.

Food and drinks (alcoholic and non-alcoholic) are available on site, plus tables and an alley bar to hang at during the event. There is a dart board and a few arcade games, as well.

**What do you do when you get there?** First, find the group inside around the front desk. Look for a growing group of people! Call or text Andy Milone at 201-234-9609 if you can't find us. Once Andy secures the lanes, please pay him before getting your bowling shoes.

**Please know that it is possible we have to wait 20-40 minutes until lane(s) free up.** It's also possible that we may have to relocate or cancel that night if there's a long wait list upon arrival. Please keep that in mind if traveling from far away!

For those who don't have cars or are looking to avoid driving, the Montvale Train Station is only like a five-minute walk from the bowling alley and can be reached via the Pascack Valley Line. Last train leaves at 12:20 a.m. and heads toward Hoboken. (https://gmtma.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/11/rail_system_map.jpg)

Many thanks to Taylor, one of our group participants, for recommending Montvale Lanes! You can learn more at: www.montvalelanes.com.

Hope you'll join us for our 24th bowling event, or consider attending one of our volleyball, ping pong, skating or other activities -> www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball

If interested in staying touch with group members or conversing about future events, feel free to inquire about our WhatsApp group chat.

description:
Roses to Rock Gardens Guest Speaker: Evan Ralph, President of Back to Nature Home & Garden 
Saturday, June 6, 9:30 AM 
 
Have you seen these signs at aspirational gardens in the area? Learn from the award-winning landscape architect behind the firm, Evan Ralph. He will share his vision and process in his talk “From Desk to Dirt: How the Design, Build and Maintenance process come together to create exceptional gardens.” 
This $15 ticket is sold separately at the ticket link and includes a light continental breakfast. Start your day with fresh garden ideas and inspiration! 
 
About Evan Ralph: 
Evan is driven by a passion for outdoor living and a deep-rooted commitment to environmental stewardship. Over the past 11 years
at Back to Nature Home & Garden, he has grown from a Landscape Designer to President, guiding the company’s evolution with
creativity, hands-on leadership, and a relentless focus on quality.
An educator at heart, he’s always ready with a pair of pruners and a willingness to teach—demonstrating what true horticulture looks
like in action. Whether he’s leading a team or tending to his own garden, his motto remains the same: “Garden, every day.” 
Back to Nature Home & Garden  
A design/build landscape architecture firm serving New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut. 
What makes Back to Nature unique is all the different offerings that we have. We’re landscape architects, we’re landscape contractors and we’re also landscape maintenance. We see opportunities where others see challenges. We design and build customized outdoor spaces that are not only beautiful, but are ecologically friendly.

location: Montclair Main - Auditorium
description:
Alliah Agostini - 4-5 p.m.

Prolific Children’s author Alliah L. Agostini reads excerpts from her stunning kids’ recipe book The Juneteenth Cookbook. She’ll go over the importance of African-American culinary traditions and why great cuisine and Juneteenth go hand-in-hand. Afterwards, kids will make their own 90’s inspired African medallion necklaces - just like in the Juneteenth Cookbook! Registration recommended for reminders and updates. 

Tobias the Horse also continues his tradition of appearing at annual Juneteenth events. Look for him on the Library lawn (Plymouth Street) and say hello between 3 to 4 pm! Tobias the Horse is graciously sponsored by Montclair Township Councilor Aminah Toler.

 

The Juneteenth Cookbook Family Challenge 

There’s nothing like families cooking together! Which is why we’re inviting children and their families to take up the Juneteenth Cookbook Family Challenge from June 1-30. Alliah L. Agostini and The Quarto Group Books have graciously granted permission to share recipes from The Juneteenth Cookbook. Kids, families, are invited to cook up any or all of the recipe items in celebration of Juneteenth. Just click the recipe links below, get cooking, and have your grownups share your creation on social media. Be sure to tag @alliago @montclairpubliclibrary and #juneteenthcookbookchallenge to join our virtual cookout!

Try to make any or all of these below recipes*:




	Jubilee Tea
	Saucy Pulled Chicken Sliders with Bangin’ Barbeque Sauce
	Red Velvet Ice Cream Sandwiches


*Excerpt © 2024 from The Juneteenth Cookbook by Alliah L. Agostini, Taffy Elrod, and Sawyer Cloud. Reproduced by permission of the publisher, becker&mayer! kids, an imprint of The Quarto Group, New York, NY.

title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: Inspiration trap creativity workshop
description:
Live African music and drumming events in NJ
6,7&8pm Issyra Gallery presents - Inspiration Trap Creativity workshop

Only 10 attendees allowed social distancing and mandatory mask wearing.

You are invited to participate in a special session of creative thinking and fresh insight dedicated to inspiration.

We live in a world of constant change that requires us to be able to continually adapt and innovate in order to succeed. Unfortunately, many of us have forgotten how to delve into our raw creativity and leave behind the rigidity of the frameworks we have progressively interiorized.
This unique workshop seeks to reclaim our inspiration and imagination, rethink the unthinkable. It is ideal for people working in the creative arts as well as students, entrepreneurs, team managers, corporate leaders and anyone looking to implement their creative vision.

Inspiration is a vital driving force in our lives that moves us to create our best work and lights the way for new, authentic ideas. How do we invite, cultivate and harness inspiration so that we are able to bring these ideas into reality?
As a self-taught artist exploring various avenues of self-expression, Issa Sow draws a distinction between the phenomenon of inspiration itself and our task of making ourselves ready for it.
In the upcoming Inspiration Trap workshop, we will imagine ways we can invite and contain our inspiration, and well as keep our mind in the open, dynamic state as a receptacle or a “canvas” to collect, reflect and grow our ideas.
Feel free to bring along a personal object, a piece of clothing or even a small piece of furniture to play with during this hands-on experiment in innovative thinking. There are surprises and new elements in each session!

Issa =2
Issa Sow is a contemporary international autodidact artist known as Issa=2.
He believes in life being a journey of continual growth with each new

title: NJ Code & Coffee - June meetup
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the monthly **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

\*your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,

* What you can help others with,
\*What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

The meetings will be held in a safe and comfortable environment where people can interact and socialize with others having similar experiences. At the gatherings participants can get support in a non-judgmental setting, while enjoying the benefits of music for the brain.

This is a joint program between Lifelong Montclair at the Township of Montclair and the Montclair Public Library.

title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: South Mountain Crest Trail
description:
Let's Walk!!
Let's Walk!! in South Mountain and visit Washington Rock and traverse a few of the many trails in the Reservation.

Washington Rock is Essex County Park System's bona fide Revolutionary War historic site, dating back to the late 1700's when Beacon Signal Station 9 was located here—one of 23 beacons built by General Washington to observe British troop movements quartered on Staten Island and New York City.

Seems like a great place to remember the nation's 250th birthday

This hike will be about 3-3.5 miles and mostly flat. The terrain is mostly dirt trails in the woods, so please wear sturdy hiking boots. **Bug spray and protective clothing is a good idea.**

Please arrive a few minutes early. We start promptly at the time posted. The hike should take us 60-90 minutes. **Please remember to bring water!**

Inclement weather may cancel this event. Please check the event page for comments prior to leaving for the meetup.

**Disclaimer:** If you join this event, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap.

*photo by Angel Madison*

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**

description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: 🥾 Let's Hike!! Jockey Hollow
description:
Let's Walk!!
Let's celebrate the nation's semiquincentennial (can you pronounce that?)

Come hike with us in the Morristown National Historic Park. We'll do about 3 miles along the Grand Parade loop, see a colonial era house and garden, and Revolutionary War soldier hut (replicas). It's a little like traveling back in time 250 years

[AllTrails: Grand Parade Loop](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/new-jersey/grand-parade-trail?u=i&sh=vgtzxk)

**PLEASE NOTE THIS WALK IS AT 09:30**
**Please arrive 5 minutes early so we can start on time.**

We've scouted these trails and find them appropriate for most of our members. If you've walked with us at Eagle Rock, this is similar in difficulty with just a little more up and down. There may be wet or muddy sections and a few rocks and tree roots. Please wear hiking boots/shoes and bring trekking poles or a walking stick, if you prefer.

Don't forget your water!

Inclement weather may cancel this event. Please check the event page for comments prior to leaving for the meetup.

**Disclaimer:** If you join this event, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap.

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
**GPS:** 40.739791, -74.289181

title: Help Desk - Bring Your Laptop, Yourself, and Your WordPress Problems
description:
WordPress Montclair Meetup
If you are running a WordPress site and are having issues and would like some help, then this Meetup is for you!

If you know some things, expert or not, and want to give back to the WordPress community, then this Meetup is for you too!

We will do our best to match a problem with a problem-solver. On-site and in real-time. Just bring yourself, your laptop, and your WordPress problems.

It's OK if you attend and only want to observe. We recognize this is how people learn. Given our time limit of two hours, we may not be able to solve everyone's issues, but we will try! If you are seeking help, please come prepared. Have your web site loaded in a browser, have your WordPress admin ready, along with a short list of issues you are trying to solve.

People helping are volunteers and may not be experts. There is risk to breaking your site! Please do not bring client or business sites that can impact reputations or revenue. If you have a staging site we can test things with, that is always preferred. If it is a production site, please create a site backup before having someone do any work on your site.

If you cannot find the group, please ask the front desk where the WordPress meetup group is meeting.

**PARKING**:
We've been asked to not park in the United Way lot behind the library as it could result in a parking ticket. Please find street parking or a parking deck.

\-\-\-
Join the **JerseyPress Slack** group to chat with others in our community and get help: [https://jerseypress.org/slack/](https://jerseypress.org/slack/)

title: Meeting at the Verona inn!
description:
Board Game Night At Verona Inn
We will be doing our first monthly meeting starting on **February 25th at the Verona Inn!** We will be meeting up to organize games starting at 7:30, with food and drinks available courtesy of our host! You can play any game provided by hosts or bring your own! If you do not have a friend group to play games, hosts will organize you into pods with other people who need players. There are **no dues**. Future meetings will be held on the **last Wednesday of each month.**

More information and ground rules:

* **The doors open at 6:30 but games do not start until 7:30.** I *highly recommend* coming in during this period to eat your food and drink ahead of time!
* **Please return the graciousness provided by our hosts and order at least one item! All venue specific rules apply to our club.** Future meetings depend on treating our hosts with respect.
* **All games must be returned to their owners when they announce that they are leaving.** If you are in a game in progress when the meeting ends but it is not borrowed you may continue playing!
* **Please place food and drink on a separate table or surface from your games** to help avoid stains and other damage.
* **Please engage with others in good faith, sportsmanship, respect and common sense.** *ABSOLUTELY NO harassment, getting physical, hurtful insulting, and persecutory language will be tolerated.* Repeat violators of venue rules AND/OR this rule may be asked to leave the event and not return.

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: Meeting at the Verona inn!
description:
Board Game Night At Verona Inn
We will be doing our first monthly meeting starting on **February 25th at the Verona Inn!** We will be meeting up to organize games starting at 7:30, with food and drinks available courtesy of our host! You can play any game provided by hosts or bring your own! If you do not have a friend group to play games, hosts will organize you into pods with other people who need players. There are **no dues**. Future meetings will be held on the **last Wednesday of each month.**

More information and ground rules:

* **The doors open at 6:30 but games do not start until 7:30.** I *highly recommend* coming in during this period to eat your food and drink ahead of time!
* **Please return the graciousness provided by our hosts and order at least one item! All venue specific rules apply to our club.** Future meetings depend on treating our hosts with respect.
* **All games must be returned to their owners when they announce that they are leaving.** If you are in a game in progress when the meeting ends but it is not borrowed you may continue playing!
* **Please place food and drink on a separate table or surface from your games** to help avoid stains and other damage.
* **Please engage with others in good faith, sportsmanship, respect and common sense.** *ABSOLUTELY NO harassment, getting physical, hurtful insulting, and persecutory language will be tolerated.* Repeat violators of venue rules AND/OR this rule may be asked to leave the event and not return.
